facts.value: Historically, equestrians honed their skills through games and races. Equestrian sports provided entertainment for crowds and honed the excellent horsemanship that was needed in battle.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: Many sports, such as dressage, eventing, and show jumping, have origins in military training, which were focused on control and balance of both horse and rider.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: Other sports, such as rodeo, developed from practical skills such as those needed on working ranches and stations. Sport hunting from horseback evolved from earlier practical hunting techniques.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: Horse racing of all types evolved from impromptu competitions between riders or drivers.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: All forms of competition, requiring demanding and specialized skills from both horse and rider, resulted in the systematic development of specialized breeds and equipment for each sport.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: The popularity of equestrian sports through the centuries has resulted in the preservation of skills that would otherwise have disappeared after horses stopped being used in combat.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: Horses are trained to be ridden or driven in a variety of sporting competitions. Examples include show jumping, dressage, three-day eventing, competitive driving, endurance riding, gymkhana, rodeos, and fox hunting.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: Horse shows, which have their origins in medieval European fairs, are held around the world. They host a huge range of classes, covering all of the mounted and harness disciplines, as well as 'In-hand' classes where the horses are led, rather than ridden, to be evaluated on their conformation.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: The method of judging varies with the discipline, but winning usually depends on style and ability of both horse and rider.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: Sports such as polo do not judge the horse itself, but rather use the horse as a partner for human competitors as a necessary part of the game.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: Although the horse requires specialized training to participate, the details of its performance are not judged, only the result of the rider's actions—be it getting a ball through a goal or some other task.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: Examples of these sports of partnership between human and horse include jousting, in which the main goal is for one rider to unseat the other, and buzkashi, a team game played throughout Central Asia, the aim being to capture a goat carcass while on horseback.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: Horse racing is an equestrian sport and major international industry, watched in almost every nation of the world.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: There are three types: 'flat' racing; steeplechasing, i.e. racing over jumps; and harness racing, where horses trot or pace while pulling a driver in a small, light cart known as a sulky.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: A major part of horse racing's economic importance lies in the gambling associated with it.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science
